summary: Postinstall downloads unverified binary from a GitHub org that does not match the declared repository
details: On install, the package's postinstall script fetches a platform-specific binary from https://github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot/releases/download/v<version>/apex-<target>, writes it to bin/apex with mode 0755, and the bin wrapper (apex.js) later spawns it with inherited stdio and the full process environment. No checksum or signature verification is performed on the downloaded bytes. The download source (Apex-Foundation/copilot) does not match the package's declared repository (can1357/oh-my-pi) or homepage (omp.sh), and the shipped README titles the package @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent — a tri-directional identity mismatch between the npm package name (@apexfdn/apex), the README, and the GitHub org that hosts the executable. If Apex-Foundation is not operated by the same maintainer as the declared repository, whoever controls that org can ship arbitrary code that runs on the installer's machine with the environment of any user who invokes the CLI. The publisher-org mismatch and README identity mismatch cannot be resolved from package contents alone and require human verification of maintainer identity.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
